reading.title: A small country, a big trader
reading.text: The Netherlands is tiny, yet it is the world's second-largest exporter of food. Its success depends on excellent transport: the port of Rotterdam receives huge volumes of imports, which are processed and sent on across Europe. The government supports farmers with research funding and cheap loans, and many companies hold a broad portfolio of products, from flowers to cheese. Critics point out that the system relies on migrant workers, some of whom are deported when their permits expire, and that moving so many goods by lorry and ship has a heavy environmental cost.
